edition_notes: Repos Production, 2025; game by Paolo Mori and Alessandro Zucchini; French-language rulebook (2-player game)

items.rule: Choose one of the 8 Terrains (the plaine des châteaux is recommended for a first game) and place it between the two players so that each player has their own Médailles objective symbol (blue or red) in front of them; this determines the Médailles objective and each player's troop color.
Place one Médaille token on each Médaille spot of the board; any leftover Médaille tokens go back in the box.
Each player places a support in front of them.
Each player shuffles all Troop tiles of their color face down to form their reserve.
Each player removes 4 Troops from their reserve without looking at them and returns them to the box; they are not used in this game.
Randomly determine the starting player. The starting player takes 3 Troops from their reserve onto their support; the opponent takes 4 Troops.
Leave an empty space next to the board for the discard pile.
For first games it is recommended to play without special base effects, treating all special bases as bases without effect.
Players alternate turns starting with the randomly chosen player; on a turn a player performs exactly one of two actions: draw 2 Troops or place 1 Troop on the board.
Action DRAW 2 TROOPS: draw 2 Troops from your reserve and put them on your support.
A support holds at most 8 Troops; you cannot take the draw action if you already have 8 Troops on your support.
If only 1 Troop remains in your reserve, or only one free slot on your support, you may still take the draw action to draw just 1 Troop.
Action PLACE 1 TROOP: choose 1 Troop from your support and place it on a location following the placement rules; you then occupy that location.
After placing, apply the Troop's effect (if any), then the effect of its base if it is a special base (see player aid).

Placement: you may place a Troop on an empty base, on a base occupied by any of your own Troops, on a base occupied by an opponent's Troop of strictly lower strength than yours, or on the opponent's HQ (never on your own HQ).

When placing on an occupied base, put the Troop on top of the existing Troop(s); a base has no limit to the number of Troops, but only the visible top Troop occupies the base. Players may look through stacks but never change their order.

Connection: the Troop must be placed on a location connected to your HQ, i.e. via a continuous path from your HQ passing only through bases you occupy; an empty base or a base occupied by an opponent interrupts the connection.
Each Troop has a strength from 1 to 7 or a joker (duck), and most also have an effect; each Troop exists in 3 copies. A 'base' includes special bases but the HQ is not a base.

Controlling a region: at any time, as soon as you occupy all the bases surrounding a region, you take control and take all Médailles in the center of that region, placing them beside your support visible to the opponent.
Médailles you took are kept until the end of the game, even if you later lose control of the region.
You can take control of several regions in the same turn; controlling a region whose Médailles were already taken gains nothing.
The game ends immediately when a player places one of their Troops on the opponent's HQ (if there are several enemy HQs, capturing one suffices).
The game ends immediately when a player reaches the number of Médailles shown on the Terrain's Médailles objective (e.g. 7).
The game also ends if a player can no longer either draw or place a Troop.
The only points are Médailles, gained by controlling regions; there is no other scoring unless the game ends by lack of actions, in which case Médaille counts are compared.
Capturing the enemy HQ gives an immediate win to the capturing player.
Reaching the Médaille objective number gives an immediate win to that player.
If the game ends because a player cannot draw or place a Troop, the player with more Médailles than the opponent wins.
If Médailles are tied when a player cannot act, the player who ended the game (the one unable to act) loses and the opponent wins.
